thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: S&P 500, Nasdaq Close Lower For Third Day In A Row As Tech Stocks Sink

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: S&P 500, Nasdaq Close Lower For Third Day In A Row As Tech Stocks Sink
text:
By Sue Chang, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Dow shakes off weakness to edge higher for 2nd session in a row
The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq finished lower for a third session Thursday on mounting concerns about contagion from a handful of struggling emerging economies on top of unresolved trade tension.
Technology stocks again weighed on the U.S. market while energy shares also fell on weak crude prices.
How did benchmarks fare?
The S&P 500 index shed 10.55 points, or 0.4%, to 2,878.05 and the Nasdaq Composite Index slid 72.45 points, or 0.9%, to 7,922.73. The Dow Jones Industrial Average erased earlier losses to rise 20.88 points to 25,995.87.
The energy sector sank 1.9%, the weakest performer of the day, while tech lost 0.8%.
What drove the market?
Turmoil in Argentina and Turkey, as their currencies continue to sink on deteriorating confidence, is dragging on the global market as investors fear a spillover effect on other healthier emerging markets and beyond.
Read:4 reasons why big-name strategists are wrong about investing in emerging markets (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/4-reasons-why-big-name-strategists-are-wrong-about-investing-in-emerging-markets-2018-09-05)
On the trade front, the U.S. and Canada continued high-stakes negotiations in the effort to revamp the North American Free Trade Agreement, which President Donald Trump said he is prepared to move forward with even without Canada's participation.
Those trade tensions come amid the start of a public comment on the Trump administration's plan to impose tariffs on an additional $200 billion of Chinese goods. Reports indicated that Trump could impose the tariffs as soon as this week.
As in Wednesday's session, there was no obvious catalyst for the drop in tech, which has been the strongest-performing sector of the year by far. The length and scale of the so-called momentum trade for the category has resulted in many analysts saying the move has been overdone.
Among notable decliners, Apple Inc. (AAPL) fell 1.7%, Google-parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) (GOOGL) dropped 1.3%, falling for a fifth session. Facebook Inc. (FB) lost 2.8%, its fourth straight daily decline.
What were analysts saying?
A team led by Marko Kolanovic, global head of macro quantitative and derivatives strategy at J.P. Morgan, blamed the weakness in global markets to a "risk-off" mode with investors seeking to minimize their exposure to risky assets such as stocks amid concerns about contagion from emerging markets as well as the impact of the stronger U.S. dollar and higher interest rates.
"This is very much a tech-centric reversion. It is long overdue, given how much the Nasdaq has been outperforming the rest of the market," said Peter Kenny, market strategist at Kenny & Co. "This is bigger than FAANG, but the scale of that move is the primary driver of what we're seeing today and what we saw yesterday. I think there's still some downside ahead, and that this won't be a short-term correction, but something that will take a long time to work through."
FAANG is an acronym that refers to a quintet of large-capitalization technology and internet stocks--Facebook, Apple, Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), Netflix Inc. (NFLX), and Google--that have sharply outperformed the broader market over the past several years.
What data were in focus?
In the latest readings on the labor market, the U.S. created 163,000 private-sector jobs in August (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/adp-us-creates-163000-private-sector-jobs-in-august-2018-09-06-81031928), according to payrolls processor ADP. This was below the 182,000 that had been expected, as well as down from July's 217,000 reading. Separately, jobless claims fell to their lowest level since 1969.
The reports come a day before the August payroll report, which is expected to show 200,000 jobs added last month.
In addition to the labor-market data, growth in U.S. productivity (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/second-quarter-us-productivity-growth-stays-at-29-2018-09-06) in the second quarter was left unchanged at 2.9% after the government's latest update.
Two reads on the services sector painted a mixed picture. The Institute for Supply Management's August read on the services sector rose to 58.5% from 55.7% in the previous month, while the final IHS Markit reading on the services purchasing managers index fell to 54.8 in August from 56 in July. Separately, a read on factory orders fell 0.8% in July.
Solid economic data in recent weeks have helped to keep the stock market on steady ground even as concerns about trade war and emerging markets cast a shadow over equities.
Read: Stock market has room to rally more than 10% by year-end, says famed bull (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-market-has-room-to-rally-more-than-10-by-year-end-says-famed-bull-2018-09-05)
Which stocks were in focus?
G-III ApparelGroup Ltd. (GIII) rose 4.5% after the owner of brands including DKNY, Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger among others, blew past earnings estimates (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dkny-parent-g-iii-apparel-shares-soar-7-premarket-after-blowout-earnings-2018-09-06) for its fiscal second quarter.
Twitter Inc.(TWTR) shares skidded 5.9% a day after Chief Executive Jack Dorsey testified on Capitol Hill (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/twitter-leads-social-media-stocks-downward-a-day-after-capitol-hill-testimony-2018-09-06) about election interference amid concerns that political provocateurs and foreign agents are using social media to manipulate the American public.
BioCryst Pharmaceuticals Inc. (BCRX) fell 4% after it said it had won a $35 million, five-year contract (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/biocryst-stock-surges-6-premarket-after-winning-35-million-cdc-contract-for-flu-therapy-2018-09-06) from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention for up to 50,000 doses of its antiviral flu therapy Rapivab.
Lands' End Inc.(LE) plunged 12.2% after the clothing and home products retailer reported a wider second-quarter loss (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/lands-ends-stock-tumbles-after-wider-loss-same-store-sales-decline-2018-09-06) and declines in same-store sales.
Navistar International Corp. (NAV) shares fell 8.5% after the company reported third-quarter results that beat expectations. It also raised its full-year revenue outlook (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/navistars-stock-rallies-after-earnings-beat-upbeat-outlook-2018-09-06).
Barnes & Noble Inc. (BKS) sank 8.1% after it reported a wider first-quarter net loss than the previous year, a fall in revenue, and a drop of 6.1% in its same-store sales.
How did other assets perform?
European stocks were mostly in the red (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-drop-as-trade-worries-persist-2018-09-05) and Asian markets closed broadly lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-mixed-though-nikkei-sags-again-2018-09-05) after a tech selloff on Wall Street. Japan's Nikkei fell 0.4%, the Shanghai Composite finished the session down 0.5%, while the Shenzhen Composite Index closed off 0.7%.
The U.S. Dollar Index remained soft (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-traders-key-in-on-jobs-data-2018-09-06), edging down 0.2% and October West Texas Intermediate crude slid more than 1% on worries about slower global demand (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-attempt-to-rebound-from-1-week-low-ahead-of-eia-weekly-inventory-report-2018-09-06).
--Mark DeCambre contributed to this article
